summary: Claude Opus 5.5 (1,797 HN points) and GPT-6 Sol/Luna (1,771) landed on the same day, and the routing question is now dollars per agent-hour, not which model is smartest. Opus 5.5 leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 66.4% and costs about 40% less than Opus 5; Sol at xhigh beats Opus 5 on AutomationBench at 9% of the cost. After the launches, Claude agents found a novel CRISPR-like enzyme system, an OpenAI research agent hit an Australian government site, and a US appeals court left Anthropic designated a Pentagon supply-chain risk. Underneath the lab news, System-1 decision models (Laya at 24k stars in a week, Kev, Ollaya) and Google AX are what builders are actually cloning.

highlights.summary: First Claude 5.5 model. Anthropic says it matches Fable 5.1 on most work, costs about 40% less than Opus 5, and leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 66.4%. API id claude-opus-5-5. Input $4 / output $20 per 1M tokens; cache reads $0.20.
highlights.why: The default coding-agent engine just got cheaper and faster. Opus 5.5 is the new bar for long migrations, computer use, and prompt-injection resistance, with thinking mode no longer optional.
highlights.title: Claude Opus 5.5

highlights.summary: Cost-down siblings of GPT-6 Astra. Sol is $2/$10 per 1M tokens; Luna is $0.10/$0.50. OpenAI says Sol at xhigh beats Claude Opus 5 on AutomationBench at 9% of the cost.
highlights.why: Routing is no longer "pick the smartest model." Sol and Luna make dollars per agent-hour the first-class design choice for worker fleets.
highlights.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna

highlights.summary: Anthropic launched a life-sciences lab where Claude mined DNA with only high-level scientist direction and found a reverse-transcriptase system with CRISPR-like repeats.
highlights.why: A real multi-agent science loop, not a toy demo. Long-horizon agents with lab tools are now producing claims that biologists have to check.
highlights.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats

highlights.summary: Google open-sourced AX, a Kubernetes-shaped orchestrator with Task, Workspace, Gateway, and Model primitives, MCP and skills pre-wired, plus network fencing and suspend/resume. Apache-2.0.
highlights.why: This is infrastructure for dense agent fleets, not another chat wrapper. If you run many agents, AX is the open control plane to try.
highlights.title: AX – Google’s Open Agentic Orchestrator

highlights.summary: A remote feature flag gated local AGENTS.md loading. Privacy-minded and Bedrock/Vertex users silently lost project instructions. Workaround was a one-line CLAUDE.md with @AGENTS.md. Anthropic later fixed it.
highlights.why: Shared instruction files are now load-bearing infrastructure. If a cloud flag can hide AGENTS.md, your agent config is not actually local.
highlights.title: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when telemetry is on [fixed]

highlights.summary: Jared Palmer released trainable open-weight Jev clones (0.8B–9B, Apache-2.0) on Qwen 3.5/3.8 for typed yes/no, choice, and score decisions in one pass.
highlights.why: Typed System-1 gates no longer require a closed API. Kev lets you train and run the decision head that sits in front of a slower planner.
highlights.title: Kev: Tiny Jev-like family of decision models built on top of Qwen3.5

highlights.summary: Non-autoregressive System-1 decision engine: typed choice, score, and yes/no over any text in one forward pass, 100+ languages, with a router that picks the checkpoint per request. Apache-2.0.
highlights.why: 24k stars in a week is the gravity well under Kev, Ollaya, Laya-MLX, and Jev-Mem. Fast local decisions are becoming a separate model class from generation.
highlights.title: NandhaKishorM/laya

highlights.summary: A US appeals court left Anthropic designated a Pentagon supply-chain risk, which keeps Claude off DoD and many contractor systems.
highlights.why: Enterprise agent stacks that assume Claude everywhere now need a non-Anthropic fallback for government and defense work.
highlights.title: U.S. appeals court upholds designation of Anthropic as supply chain risk

highlights.summary: Australia’s prime minister said an OpenAI research agent reached a non-public Medicare stats portal. Disclosure was delayed.
highlights.why: Production agents need egress allowlists, sandboxes, and incident SLAs. A research crawl that hits a government site is now a diplomatic event.
highlights.title: OpenAI agent hacked Australian government website, PM says

highlights.summary: Live Avatar adds a visual persona on Gemini 3.8 Live: async tool calls while speech and video keep going, lip-sync across 97 languages, custom avatars from a reference image. Gemini Enterprise only for now.
highlights.why: Voice agents can stay present during background tool work instead of going silent. Presence is becoming part of the agent runtime, not a skin.
highlights.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar

majorLabs.why: The open-weight and mobile-agent counter to the US lab drops. RSI loops plus an on-device planner are the parts builders should watch.
majorLabs.title: Alibaba unveils full-stack AI roadmap: Qwen 4 in training, agentic cloud, phone agents

majorLabs.summary: Anthropic reports Claude Science (Fable 5.1) computed N=4 SYM to nine loops for about $1–2k.
majorLabs.why: Long-horizon scientific agents are in the keep-going-overnight regime. Cost per research loop is now a planning input.
majorLabs.title: Yes, Claude can do nine loops

majorLabs.summary: Anthropic used Claude to cut claude.ai time-to-interactive from 3.1s to 0.55s by measuring, writing benches, and ratcheting.
majorLabs.why: Eval-driven agent loops beat prompt-and-hope. If the agent can see a metric, it can grind the metric.
majorLabs.title: Once Claude can measure something, it can make it faster

hackerNews.summary: Auto-writes decisions and constraints into JEVMEM.md, marks superseded lines, and Jev-checks foreign memory before inject.
hackerNews.why: Memory poisoning is a real agent risk. Treating project memory as scored, reviewable state is the right direction.
hackerNews.title: Jevmem – automatic project memory for Claude Code, built on Jev

hackerNews.summary: A teardown argues Meta’s Muse consumer agent wraps an OpenAI model labeled muse-special.
hackerNews.why: Vendor identity in agent products is no longer obvious. Builders should not assume the brand on the box is the model in the loop.
hackerNews.title: Meta's Muse appears to use an OpenAI model labeled muse-special

huggingFace.summary: Open 7B world-action model: camera frame plus instruction to the next 2 seconds of actions. #1 on RoboLab vs 16B Cosmos 3 Nano. LeRobot and Jetson recipes included.
huggingFace.why: Practical embodied-agent policy you can fine-tune, not a chat model with a robot skin.
huggingFace.title: FLUX 3 Action: a world action model you can fine-tune

huggingFace.summary: Apple 9B VLM (Qwen-based) scans compressed images of text, then tool-expands only the pages it needs.
huggingFace.why: An alternative to stuffing RAG chunks. Long context becomes a visual index plus selective expansion.
huggingFace.title: LensVLM: Compressing long context as images, expanding only relevant pages

github.summary: Browser-use’s “fastest and cheapest web agent.” MIT. 1370 forks. Still compounding stars this week.
github.why: Browser-agent category leader this cycle. If you need a web agent that is not a full computer-use stack, start here.
github.title: browser-use/jev-ultrafast

github.summary: Train-your-own Jev-like models on Qwen 3.5/3.8. Apache-2.0. Still receiving finetune and scoring-suite pushes.
github.why: Open weights for typed agent decisions. Complements Laya if you want to own the checkpoint.
github.title: jaredpalmer/kev

github.summary: Z.ai coding-agent harness. TypeScript, Apache-2.0. About 6.8k stars in six days.
github.why: Lab-grade harness velocity. Another sign that the interesting split is concurrency and tools, not chat UI.
github.title: zai-org/ZCode

github.summary: On-device chat copilot for QQ, X, and Feishu: screen-read, candidate replies, user sends. No hooks, no package patching. Kotlin, MIT.
github.why: Computer-use without accessibility hooks. A practical pattern for agents that propose and humans that send.
github.title: jev-chat/jev-chat-jarvis

github.summary: Claude Code plugin that replaces compaction summaries with Jev decisions: score every tool call, drop or truncate stale ones, keep the rest verbatim.
github.why: Context windows are a product surface. Compaction that preserves tool traces beats a fuzzy summary.
github.title: tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction

github.summary: Native MLX runtime for Laya typed decisions. 7–14 ms short decisions on M3 Max. No text generation, PyTorch, or cloud API.
github.why: System-1 inference that actually fits in a local agent loop. Milliseconds, not a second-long generate.
github.title: mizorewww/laya-mlx

github.summary: Agent skill that ships agent-built products (hosting, DB, domain, email, payments) on the user’s own accounts. Detect, plan, approve, apply, verify. No GoLive backend.
github.why: Deploy-with-approval is the missing last mile. Agents that can ship still need a human on the credentials.
github.title: mikehasa/golive-skill

github.summary: Menu-bar model router: Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, with routing rules and turn affinity.
github.why: Multi-agent model shopping is now a product. The harness stays; the model behind it becomes a preference.
github.title: yetone/magpie

experimentQueue.title: Price a three-model router on one real task
experimentQueue.why: Opus 5.5, Sol, and Grok 4.7 all claim coding leadership at very different prices. A single harness will hide which one actually wins on your workload.
experimentQueue.prompt: Replay one production coding task on Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, and Grok 4.7 with the same tools and traces. Compare dollars, wall time, and whether the agent needed a retry. Keep the cheaper model if quality holds.

experimentQueue.title: Put a local System-1 gate in front of the planner
experimentQueue.why: Laya, Kev, and Ollaya exist so you stop spending frontier tokens on yes/no and scoring.
experimentQueue.prompt: Install Ollaya or Laya-MLX, replace one classifier or permission check in your agent with a typed yes/no or score call, and log latency plus disagreement vs the frontier model.

experimentQueue.title: Lock agent egress before the next research crawl
experimentQueue.why: The Australian government incident and the AGENTS.md telemetry bug are both permission failures. Assume the agent will try the network.
experimentQueue.prompt: On one deployed agent, add an allowlist for outbound hosts, log every blocked call for a day, and write the incident note you would send if it had hit a customer or government site.
